headline: Recommended a minimum LEED v4 Silver standard for the Medford High project; approved moving middle school grade reconfiguration to SY 28-29.
summary: The meeting covered Medford High School building storage, a Japanese Language School partnership, a teen health center, sustainability goals, and school rules changes. Members approved moving middle school grade reconfiguration to SY 28-29 and a resolution thanking state legislators for $632,000 in school funding. They also approved resolution 2026-19 as amended and tabled the rules changes until August.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including bills, payrolls, and minutes of the June 15, 2026 and July 10, 2026 meetings, 7-0.
Approved moving the go-live date of middle school grade reconfiguration to SY 28-29 instead of SY 27-28, 6-0 with Graham absent.
Approved a motion to not build any storage space for rental use in the new MHS, 6-0 with Graham absent.
Approved a motion that the facilities subcommittee will meet to discuss the storage situation at the McGlynn, 6-0 with Graham absent.
Recommended that the SBC continue to maintain a teen health center space, 5-0 with Mayor abstaining and Graham absent.

Recommended that the Medford High School project achieve a minimum of LEED v4 Silver certification to meet MSBA requirements, while prioritizing building performance, occupant health, and lifecycle cost over point accumulation, 5-0 with Mayor abstaining and Graham absent.
Tabled the proposed amendments to the Rules of the School Committee (2026-06) until the August meeting, 6-0 with Graham abstaining.

Approved resolution 2026-17 directing the Curriculum & Instruction subcommittee to meet with the Assistant Superintendent for Academics & Instruction by October 15 on alignment with the K-12 Statewide Graduation Council's recommendations, 6-0 with Graham absent.
Approved resolution 2026-18 thanking the Medford State Legislative Delegation for $632,000 in additional funding for Medford Public Schools, 6-0 with Graham absent.

Approved resolution 2026-19 on students, families, and staff affected by TPS terminations, as amended to add "Make reasonable efforts to ensure that all MPS students have emergency contacts on file." between items 2 and 3, 6-0 with Graham absent.
